ground.

options.text: the same as that at Y

options.text: It obtains its energy from the Sun.

pressure of the air inside the container.
What causes the increase in pressure of the air inside the container?

questions.questionText:
A very hot mug of coffee is near a large unheated swimming pool holding 2.0  106kg of water.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: If the mug of coffee is tipped in the pool, the coffee will lose much more internal energy than the water in the pool gains.
The internal energy of a substance depends only on its temperature.
The internal energy of the water in the pool is lower than the internal energy of the mug of coffee.
When the temperature of the mug of coffee falls, its internal energy will decrease.

time/hours mass of water/g

A 1kg block of aluminium requires more thermal energy to raise its temperature by 1C than a
1kg block of copper requires.
Why is this?

options.text: Aluminium is a better conductor of thermal energy than copper.
Aluminium is a poorer conductor of thermal energy than copper.
Aluminium has a higher specific heat capacity than copper.
Aluminium has a lower specific heat capacity than copper.

-particles are directed at a metal foil.
Most of the particles pass through the foil with little change in direction.

options.text: It consists of a charged centre much smaller than the size of the atom and with little of the mass of the atom.
It consists of a negative charge the size of the atom containing small positive charges scattered through it.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly compares the properties of alpha-particles and beta-particles?

options.text: Alpha-particles are less penetrating than beta-particles because alpha-particles are less ionising.
Alpha-particles are less penetrating than beta-particles because alpha-particles are more ionising.
Alpha-particles are more penetrating than beta-particles because alpha-particles are less ionising.
Alpha-particles are more penetrating than beta-particles because alpha-particles are more ionising.

questions.questionText: Which statement about alpha decay is correct?

options.text: The nucleus changes to that of a different element.
The nucleus does not decay until after one half-life.
After two half-lives, alpha decay always stops.

questions.questionText: Which type of object rotates around the Sun with an elliptical orbit?
Which statement about the Sun is correct?

options.text: The nuclear reactions in the Sun create mainly radio waves and microwaves.
The Sun is powered by fission reactions in which hydrogen is converted into helium.
The Sun is powered by fission reactions in which lithium is converted into helium.
The Sun is powered by fusion reactions and electromagnetic radiation is produced.
